steps.title: Prepare slicing and recording solutions
steps.instruction: Make 500 mL slicing solution (230 mM sucrose, 26 mM NaHCO₃, 2.5 mM KCl, 1.25 mM NaH₂PO₄·H₂O, 10 mM MgSO₄, 0.5 mM CaCl₂, 10 mM glucose, bring to 500 mL with dH₂O), keep at 4 °C and continuously carbonate with 95 % O₂/5 % CO₂. Prepare 1 L ACSF (134 mM NaCl, 2.5 mM KCl, 1.3 mM MgCl₂, 2 mM CaCl₂, 1.26 mM K₂HPO₄, 26 mM NaHCO₃, 10 mM glucose, bring to 1 L with dH₂O), keep at room temperature, carbonate (95 % O₂/5 % CO₂) and store up to one week at 4 °C. Prepare 1 L ACSF with 1 µM Sulforhodamine 101 (add 0.0006 g SR101), keep at 35 °C, carbonate, aliquot 250 mL for slice storage and 75 mL for incubation; all solutions must be carbonated at least 15 min before use.

substeps.instruction: a. Prepare 500 mL slicing solution, cool to 4 °C, carbonate.
b. Prepare 1 L ACSF, carbonate, place 250 mL in 300 mL beaker with nylon chambers for slice storage.
c. Prepare or thaw 1 L ACSF + SR101, carbonate, place 75 mL in 100 mL glass beaker with nylon chamber, warm to 35 °C.

steps.title: Set up vibratome and surgical tools
steps.instruction: Switch on the vibratome, install a fresh X10 double‑sided razor blade, set thickness = 250 µm, frequency = 90, amplitude = 1.0. Gather large scissors for decapitation, small scissors, tweezers, spatula, reusable blade, and a cut‑tip Pasteur pipette. Prepare a 10 cm Ø glass Petri dish filled with ice and place a cut piece of filter paper on the ice.

substeps.instruction: a. Turn on vibratome and mount blade.
b. Set vibratome parameters (250 µm, 90, 1.0).
c. Assemble surgical equipment and ice‑cold Petri dish.

steps.title: Dissect mouse brain and mount for slicing
steps.instruction: Euthanize mouse by cervical dislocation and decapitate with large scissors. Cut skin from caudal base toward nose, make two parallel cuts on each side of the skull from caudal to rostral meeting between the eyes, peel away skull with forceps, extract brain with a spatula, briefly immerse brain in ice‑cold slicing solution, place brain on filter paper in the chilled Petri dish, remove brainstem, make an antero‑posterior nick on one cortical side as a landmark, glue the frontal side up onto the vibratome specimen holder with superglue, insert holder into the slicing chamber, fill chamber with ice‑cold slicing solution and continue carbonate.

substeps.instruction: a. Sacrifice mouse and decapitate.
b. Remove skin and make parallel skull cuts.
c. Peel skull and extract brain.
d. Place brain in ice‑cold slicing solution briefly.
e. Transfer brain to filter paper on ice.
f. Remove brainstem and make cortical nick.
g. Glue brain (frontal side up) to specimen holder.
h. Insert holder into slicing chamber.
i. Fill chamber with ice‑cold slicing solution and carbonate.

steps.title: Cut coronal slices and collect
steps.instruction: Using the vibratome settings from step 2, cut 250 µm coronal slices until the region of interest is reached; discard rostral thick slices if not needed. Transfer each slice with a cut Pasteur pipette into a holding chamber containing carbonated ACSF at room temperature. Slices may be stored up to 5 h.

substeps.instruction: a. Cut 250 µm slices with vibratome.
b. Discard unwanted rostral slices.
c. Transfer slices to ACSF holding chamber (RT).
d. Store slices ≤5 h.

steps.title: SR101 pre‑labeling of slices
steps.instruction: Place a single slice into the incubator containing 75 mL ACSF + SR101 at 35 °C for 20 min. Incubate slices one at a time; do not start the next slice until the previous slice has been patched and dye‑loaded.

substeps.instruction: a. Incubate slice 20 min at 35 °C in ACSF + SR101.
b. Process slices sequentially.

steps.title: Prepare patch‑clamp setup and intracellular solution
steps.instruction: Turn on all equipment and run ACSF at room temperature through the patch‑clamp chamber using a peristaltic pump with Tygon tubing. Thaw a 1 mL aliquot of intracellular solution (ICS) or take from fridge, filter through a Millex 0.22 µm filter unit, then add fresh 0.5 % biocytin (0.005 mg) and Lucifer Yellow (10 µg/mL) immediately before use.

substeps.instruction: a. Power on equipment and flow ACSF (RT).
b. Thaw and filter ICS solution.
c. Add biocytin and Lucifer Yellow.

steps.title: Transfer slice to recording chamber
steps.instruction: Using a cut glass Pasteur pipette, move the incubated slice into the patch‑clamp recording chamber and anchor it with a platinum harp grid and nylon threads.

steps.title: Locate and identify fluorescent astrocyte
steps.instruction: With the 5× objective, move the stage (Scientifica control panel) to the region of interest. Switch to the 60× water‑immersion objective, excite SR101 at 555 nm (±10 nm) and detect emission at 585 nm (±10 nm) using the monochromator. Choose a fluorescent cell at least a few microns below the slice surface; avoid moving the x‑ or y‑axes after selection.

steps.title: Pull and fill recording pipette
steps.instruction: Pull a borosilicate glass pipette (1.5 mm OD, 0.315 mm wall) to obtain 4–8 MΩ resistance. Fill with 5–10 µL of ICS + biocytin, mount on the micromanipulator, and apply 0.1 mL positive pressure with a 1 mL syringe to generate outflow. Verify outflow by switching to the Lucifer Yellow filter (excitation 495 nm, emission 510 ± 10 nm).

substeps.instruction: a. Pull pipette to 4–8 MΩ.
b. Fill with 5–10 µL ICS + biocytin.
c. Mount pipette and apply positive pressure.
d. Confirm Lucifer Yellow outflow.

steps.title: Approach selected astrocyte
steps.instruction: Lower the pipette into the bath slowly, keeping the tip above the slice. Apply a test pulse (single –10 mV step) via the HEKA amplifier and TIDA software; confirm a stable resistance (R‑Mem). Move the pipette toward the slice until the tip is just above the focal plane, monitor Lucifer Yellow outflow, and compensate offset (V0Auto).

substeps.instruction: a. Lower pipette into bath.
b. Apply –10 mV test pulse and check resistance.
c. Advance pipette to just above slice focal plane.
d. Verify Lucifer Yellow outflow.
e. Compensate offset (V0Auto).

steps.title: Form gigaseal and whole‑cell configuration
steps.instruction: Touch the pipette to the cell membrane; observe a dimple and a 0.2–0.4 MΩ increase in resistance. Release positive pressure and apply 0.05–0.2 mL negative pressure to reach several hundred MΩ, then continue suction until a gigaseal (>1 GΩ) forms. Apply a brief suction pulse (by syringe or mouth) to break into whole‑cell; observe an abrupt increase in capacitive transient amplitude.

substeps.instruction: a. Lightly touch cell membrane.
b. Remove positive pressure, apply negative pressure.
c. Achieve gigaseal (>1 GΩ).
d. Apply brief suction to obtain whole‑cell.

steps.title: Record voltage steps to verify astrocyte
steps.instruction: Run a voltage‑step protocol: hold at –70 mV, apply steps from –160 mV to +50 mV in 10 mV increments, each 50 ms, filtered at 2.9 kHz. Confirm low input resistance typical of astrocytes.

steps.title: Image dye‑filled network
steps.instruction: Using a confocal microscope (Leica DM TCS SPE), acquire a low‑magnification (5×) image (excitation/emission 554/566 nm) to locate the Cy3‑streptavidin signal. Switch to a 20× objective and record a z‑stack from the deepest to the shallowest plane with 1 µm step size. Adjust laser power, gain, etc., and also acquire DAPI and GFAP channels. Analyze stacks with Fiji/ImageJ (cell counter plugin and z‑projection) to determine network size.

substeps.instruction: a. Capture 5× overview (Cy3‑streptavidin).
b. Record 20× z‑stack (1 µm steps).
c. Acquire additional fluorescence channels.
d. Analyze with Fiji/ImageJ.
